title: granular-background-reclaim-and-slowpath-allocation-optimizer
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: reduce tail-latency spikes caused by allocator slowpaths and coarse-grained background reclaim during high-concurrency KV workloads. This PR introduces a granular background reclaim scheduler, prioritizes light-weight fastpath allocations, and adds a 'cohort' soft-pinning heuristic to prevent repeated churn of hot blocks. Approach: (1) BackgroundReclaimer: break global reclaim into per-shard micro-epochs that can be paused/rate-limited by latency SLO signals; (2) Fastpath reservations: a small per-worker reservation pool ensures common small allocations avoid slowpath locking; (3) Cohort soft-pin: track recent hot-block cohorts and apply a decaying soft-pin score instead of strict pin, enabling opportunistic reuse while avoiding long-lived hard pins; (4) Slowpath optimizer: when a slowpath allocation is required we attempt quick-steal from low-scored cohorts before escalating to full reclaim; (5) Runtime signal hooks: reclaim aggressiveness responds to sampled 99th token latency and queue depth. Rollout: behind feature-flag kv.bg_reclaim_granular=true and default-off for dedicated until smoke and canaries pass. Testing: unit tests for cohort scoring and reservation under concurrency, integration e2e with continuous-batching harness, perf bench harness added. Impact: reduces spikey allocation latency and improves token throughput under load with mixed sequence lengths. Risks: tuning parameters could under-reclaim in long-running workloads; feature gated and has emergency kill-switch. Checklist: - design doc linked; - microbench and canary results attached; - docs note for ops flags; - migration strategy for persisted metadata. Related: builds on ENG-2024 allocator refactor and ties into runtime scheduling work in ENG-2642.
commits_summary: 5 commits: initial granular reclaimer scaffold; implement per-shard micro-epochs; add fastpath reservation pool and APIs; cohort scoring and soft-pin; tests, benchmarks, and docs updates; final cleanup and lint fixes.
review_comments: Kai Huang: Can we quantify the CPU overhead of per-shard epochs? Suggest adding a sampled CPU profile under canary. Author: added microbench and included cost budget in docs.
Marta Svensson: Cohort scoring looks promising, but ensure decay constants are configurable. Author: expose decay, min_score and scan windows in flags with safe defaults.
Diego Romero (SRE): Add metrics for reclaim preemptions and slowpath steal counts for alerts. Author: added kv_reclaim.preemptions and kv_reclaim.steal_count metrics and wired to console.
Kai Huang: found a race in reservation pool resize under rapid worker start/stop. Author: fixed with CAS-backed resize and added regression test.

benchmarks: reported (see bench artifacts, p99 allocation latency down ~42% on mix-96 workload)
canary-smoke: pass (staged rollout to 5% dogfood cluster)
release_notes: Performance: introduced granular background reclaim and fastpath reservations to reduce allocation tail latency and improve token throughput under mixed workloads. Ops: new feature flags kv.bg_reclaim_granular and kv.fastpath_reservations; tuning guidance in ops docs.
